case_study_insert.main_stem: Hollowbrook Bearings (HBB) is a public limited company in the industrial bearing manufacturing sector, employing a workforce of 120. Founded in 2004 by Nadia Hollowbrook in Penang, the business supplies sealed ball bearings to automotive and wind-turbine assemblers and operates a hierarchical structure with autocratic leadership and tight lean-production targets. HBB plans to invest $1,200,000 in an automated bearing-race grinding cell, financed by a $400,000 share issue and an $800,000 five-year bank loan. It has fixed costs of $480,000 a year, a variable cost of $12.00 a unit and a selling price of $28.00, and currently produces 120,000 units a year. HBB faces rising labour turnover and an increase in scrap waste on the older grinding lines.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Operations and Quality Report — Q3 2025: The bearing line produced 30,000 units last quarter at a scrap rate of 3.2%, up from 2.1% a year ago, and logged 26 customer warranty complaints per month. Average delivery lead time is 9 days. A survey of 450 procurement managers found that 72% rank product reliability as the main purchase criterion, while 38% would pay a 4% premium for longer-life bearings. A skills audit shows 22 of 120 workers are not certified after on-the-job training on the new race grinders; off-the-job training at the vocational institute costs $1,200 per employee.

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (October 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 5.0% to 5.8%, the third rise this year, lifting borrowing costs on variable-rate company debt. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 5.5% from $11.80 to $12.45 per hour from April 2026. (3) Imported alloy steel and bearing Input costs have risen 9.6% year-on-year after a sharp fall in the exchange rate, while industrial energy prices are up 6.2%.

questions.question_text: HBB plans to fund part of its $1,200,000 automated grinding cell with a $400,000 share issue. Explain two advantages for HBB of using this share issue instead of more bank borrowing.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: A $400,000 share issue brings in permanent equity that needs no interest or repayment, which protects cash flow while HBB already carries fixed costs of $480,000 a year and an $800,000 five-year bank loan. Unlike extra debt, there is no collateral to pledge, so the existing bearing plant is not at risk if the 3.2% scrap rate delays the new cell's payback, and the money can absorb the 9.6% rise in alloy steel costs.

Point 2: Equity improves the financial position shown in Appendix 2 by raising capital employed without adding current liabilities, giving HBB more headroom with lenders and helping it keep supplying automotive and wind-turbine assemblers. Although existing shareholders are diluted, a public limited company can access a wide investor market; the funds let Nadia Hollowbrook proceed with the $1,200,000 investment without the repossession risk that would accompany a larger loan, which matters when 72% of procurement managers rank reliability above all else.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to HBB's share issue, loan and expansion.

questions.question_text: HBB is launching a new longer-life sealed bearing. Consider sponsoring an industry conference, employing a direct technical sales team, or promoting through an e-commerce website with online search advertising. Which should HBB choose? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Industry conference sponsorship: Sponsoring a wind-energy or automotive conference puts HBB in front of the exact assemblers it supplies and allows engineers to inspect samples, supported by research showing 72% of 450 buyers rank reliability first. However, sponsorship is a one-off event with high, lumpy cost and limited reach, and it does not by itself demonstrate the longer-life performance that the 38% willing to pay a 4% premium would need to see.

Direct technical sales team: A team of engineers visiting procurement managers can give detailed specifications, negotiate contracts and build relationships for high-value sealed bearings, which suits a hierarchical, target-driven business. The downside is high fixed salary and travel cost for a firm already servicing an $800,000 loan, and a small team can cover only a fraction of potential automotive and turbine accounts, making growth slow.

E-commerce website and online search advertising: A technical website with specification sheets and pay-per-click search ads reaches buyers actively looking for bearings, can show reliability data to the 72% who value it, and is measurable and scalable at modest cost while supporting the 9-day delivery lead time.

Recommendation: HBB should choose the e-commerce website with online search advertising as its main channel, backed by occasional conference presence. Online promotion is targeted, measurable and cheaper than a permanent sales team, unlike conference sponsorship it works continuously, and the 38% premium segment can be shown longer-life data directly. A large direct sales force is rejected as too costly against a $1,200,000 investment and an $800,000 loan.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited outline of the promotional options with minimal context.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discussion of advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in the context of HBB with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed discussion of all three options in the context of HBB with a well-justified recommendation explaining why the other two are secondary.

questions.question_text: HBB has an autocratic leadership style and rising labour turnover. Explain two benefits for HBB of this autocratic leadership in its bearing plant.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Autocratic leadership lets Nadia Hollowbrook set clear lean-production targets and make fast decisions, which suits a hierarchical plant producing 120,000 bearings a year where the 3.2% scrap rate must be brought under control. Unambiguous instructions and tight supervision reduce confusion on the older grinding lines, help hold the 9-day delivery lead time, and give the 72% of buyers who rank reliability first a consistent product.

Point 2: Centralised decisions allow rapid standardisation of work methods across the 120 workforce, so when 22 workers need certification on the new grinders the required routines can be imposed quickly without lengthy consultation. This can raise labour productivity of 120,000 units ÷ 120 staff = 1,000 units per worker and contain the $1,200-per-employee training bill, addressing the labour turnover problem by making roles and expectations explicit in a factory where precision matters.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to HBB's scrap rate, structure and output.

questions.question_text: HBB must certify 22 of its 120 workers on the new race grinders. Consider on-the-job training or off-the-job training at the vocational institute. Which should HBB choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Coaching on HBB's own race grinders is directly relevant to the 3.2% scrap problem and the firm's lean standards, costs no course fees and keeps the 22 workers producing bearings while they learn, protecting the 30,000 units made last quarter. Its weaknesses are that supervisor-trainers lose output, bad habits may spread, and there is no external certificate, yet for a hierarchical plant the firm's own method may be exactly what supervisors want to enforce.

Off-the-job training: The vocational institute course at $1,200 per employee costs $26,400 for 22 workers, affordable beside a $1,200,000 investment, and delivers structured skills plus a recognised certificate that supports the reliability message to the 72% of buyers who rank it first. It takes 22 of 120 staff off the line, however, threatening the 9-day lead time, and the generic content may not match HBB's exact grinder settings without follow-up coaching.

Decision: HBB should choose off-the-job training for the 22 workers, followed by short on-the-job refreshes. The certificate underpins the longer-life reliability claim that 38% of buyers will pay a 4% premium for, and $26,400 is small against the investment. Pure on-the-job training is rejected because it cannot credibly certify staff or cut the 3.2% scrap rate as visibly, while the temporary capacity loss can be managed with lean scheduling.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to HBB.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of benefits and drawbacks of both methods in the context of HBB.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both methods in context with a well-justified decision covering certification, cost and disruption.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how HBB's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $480,000 ÷ ($28.00 − $12.00) = $480,000 ÷ $16.00 = 30,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 30,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $28.00 − $12.00 = $16.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $16.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways HBB's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare the 30,000-unit break-even output with actual output of 120,000 units, a margin of safety of 90,000 units, to confirm the bearing range can absorb the $1,200,000 automated cell before volume is committed.
2. Use the $16.00 contribution per unit to test the 4% premium for longer-life bearings: a 4% rise on $28.00 adds about $1.12 per unit, so managers can quantify the benefit against $480,000 fixed costs.
3. Set output targets to service the $800,000 bank loan from contribution, checking the new grinders generate enough volume to justify the $1,200,000 investment.
4. Monitor unit cost ($480,000 ÷ 120,000 units + $12.00 = $16.00) each quarter to detect the 3.2% scrap waste and the impact of 9.6% alloy steel inflation, prompting supplier negotiations.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 30,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $16.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses: margin of safety of 90,000 units vs 120,000 output; modelling the 4% premium at $16.00 contribution; loan-service volume for the $1,200,000 cell; and unit-cost tracking at $16.00 to attack 3.2% scrap.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method and 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate HBB's financial position by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has HBB's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.50 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 1.61 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 0.95 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 1.11 : 1

Detailed workings: 2024 current assets = $220,000 inventories + $300,000 trade receivables + $80,000 cash = $600,000; 2025 current assets = $180,000 + $340,000 + $60,000 = $580,000. Dividing by current liabilities gives 2024 $600,000 ÷ $400,000 and 2025 $580,000 ÷ $360,000. Excluding inventories, liquid assets are 2024 ($600,000 − $220,000) = $380,000 and 2025 ($580,000 − $180,000) = $400,000, divided by the same current liabilities to give the four figures stated above.

Evaluation: Liquidity has improved. The first measure rose from 1.50 to 1.61 because current liabilities fell from $400,000 to $360,000 faster than current assets declined, so short-term obligations are better covered. The second measure, which removes stock, improved from 0.95 to 1.11 as inventories were cut from $220,000 to $180,000, meaning HBB relies less on selling bearings to meet debts — valuable while it services an $800,000 loan and a $1,200,000 investment. Nevertheless, trade receivables rose from $300,000 to $340,000 and cash fell from $80,000 to $60,000, so if automotive or turbine assemblers delay payment the apparent strength could reverse quickly, and tighter credit control is needed.

Conclusion: HBB's financial position has improved. Both liquidity measures moved favourably (1.50 to 1.61 and 0.95 to 1.11) and the gain is not inventory-dependent. The main residual weakness is higher receivables and lower cash, so collection should be prioritised before further expansion.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates both ratios for 2024 and 2025 with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years with detailed evaluation of inventories, receivables, cash and liabilities and a justified conclusion on improvement.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for HBB of using inspection-based quality control to reduce its 3.2% scrap rate.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Inspecting finished bearings lets HBB detect and reject faulty units before they reach automotive and wind-turbine assemblers, directly tackling the 3.2% scrap rate and the 26 warranty complaints per month. With autocratic leadership and hierarchical supervision, inspection rules can be enforced consistently, protecting the reliability record that 72% of 450 buyers rank as their main purchase criterion and supporting the longer-life bearing that 38% would pay a 4% premium for.

Disadvantage: Inspection happens after defects are made, so the 3.2% scrap and its material cost are already incurred, and hiring inspectors adds to fixed costs of $480,000 a year while the $800,000 loan is serviced. Inspection can also slow the 9-day delivery lead time if batches queue for checking, and it does not find the root cause on the older grinders, so the 3.2% scrap rate may persist and the $1,200,000 new cell could inherit the same problem.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to HBB's scrap rate, complaints and leadership style.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 5.8%, the 5.5% minimum wage increase and the 9.6% rise in alloy steel costs will affect HBB. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (5.0% to 5.8%): If HBB's $800,000 five-year bank loan is variable-rate, the annual interest cost rises by 0.8% of $800,000 = $6,400 a year (0.008 × $800,000). That is modest next to fixed costs of $480,000, and if the loan is fixed-rate there is no direct increase. Higher rates may also cool automotive and wind-turbine investment and raise the cost of future funding beyond the $1,200,000 cell, but HBB can limit the damage by fixing the loan rate.

Minimum wage increase (5.5%, to $12.45 per hour): With a workforce of 120, many packing and support roles are likely hourly-paid, so this rise lifts the wage bill and cannot be avoided. The insert gives no hours worked or individual pay, so a defensible annual total cannot be invented; the sound comparison is with the given productivity of 120,000 units ÷ 120 staff = 1,000 units per worker. Unless that productivity is maintained or output rises, unit labour cost climbs and the $16.00 contribution per unit narrows, especially while labour turnover is a problem.

Alloy steel input inflation (9.6%): HBB's variable cost of $12.00 per unit includes materials, but the insert does not decompose it, so only a labelled bound is honest: if the full $12.00 rose 9.6% it would add 9.6% × $12.00 = $1.15 per unit, roughly $138,000 a year at 120,000 units, driving contribution from $16.00 toward $14.85. The 38% of surveyed buyers willing to pay a 4% premium offers only partial recovery, since reliability not price dominates for 72%.

Conclusion: The 9.6% alloy steel rise will have the greatest impact because it applies to every one of the 120,000 bearings and directly erodes the $16.00 contribution that supports the $1,200,000 investment. The loan rise is at most $6,400 a year and the wage effect depends on unstated hours and can be offset by productivity, so both are smaller or less certain than pervasive material inflation.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external factors with limited application to HBB.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on HBB's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three external changes in context with a well-justified judgment that input-cost inflation has the greatest impact and why the others are smaller.
